title: Jackson State, Cameron College and Jim Hill school
summary: Names of Jackson's Black schools and colleges and the Reconstruction figures they were named for.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: I don't know the name of the college. It's a ....(?). .... college. But it's the only Black college in Meridian, or they only have one... They used to have two in Jackson. There was Cameron College and Jackson College. But when the state took over Jackson and made it Jackson
State, then they bought up the Cameron College properties which were down the street a little ways and across the street, and made it all a part of Jackson State.

Now, Jackson State College was located on Lynch Street, the same street that my first school was located on -- and it was called Jim Hill. We went from the First Grade through the Ninth Grade at Jim Hill. And some time later, I found out that Jim Hill had been the Secretary of the State of Mississippi during the Reconstruction period. And also, I found out after I got to California that John R. Lynch was the man that Lynch Street was named after, and he was also a Congressman, a Black Congressman during the Reconstruction period.
